key_insight: Strong lateral confinement can restore sustained large-scale circulation reversals in very low-Prandtl-number liquid-metal convection by inducing a plume-condensation transition that preserves buoyancy transport.
engineering_relevance: This suggests confinement geometry can be used as a practical control knob for thermal mixing and flow directionality in liquid-metal cooling and other low-Pr convection systems.
method: Direct numerical simulations of liquid-metal convection at Pr = 0.029
Systematic variation of lateral confinement to probe reversal behavior
Thermal dissipation analysis to link plume coherence with buoyancy delivery
evidence_signal: The simulations identify a distinct "island of reversal" in parameter space and show that confined flows organize into coherent plume structures associated with sustained LSC reversals.
watch_item: The reversal mechanism appears sensitive to geometry and confinement strength, so the result may not generalize to all low-Pr convection configurations without further validation.
paper_title: Flow Reversal in Low-Prandtl-Number Convection via Lateral Confinement
